newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower, freeze premium disappears.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower, freeze premium disappears.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower amid growing bearish sentiment on technicals and improving crop prospects in the U.S., Australia and Europe, although commercial buying limited losses, floor sources said.
"Wheat had a fairly important technical breakdown," said Dave Armstrong, analyst with ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp. "It closed below the post-freeze low of $4.14 (on the July contract)."
July finished 5-1/4 cents a bushel lower at $4.11-1/4.
A sharp drop in temperatures during the weekend of April 12/13 led to a sharp rise in prices but dealers noted the market had now lost its "frost premium."

A tour organized by the Wheat Quality Council through Kansas wheat fields this week should provide further indication on the extent of freeze damage. Prices may fall further if the state's crop appears in reasonable shape.
"The risk (of a further drop in prices) is there if they talk about how good everything is outside the freeze areas," Armstrong said.
Rains in Europe and Australia over the weekend also improved crop prospects in those areas.
In the export market Pakistan was tendering for 330,000 tonnes of wheat from either the U.S. or Australia on Tuesday.
Volume on wheat was estimated at 20,000 contracts, down from 23,069 on Friday.
